reason: B's Princeville base reaches the north shore cleanly (Kilauea Point, Anini, Hanalei Bay, Kalalau Trail to Hanakapiai on day 7), whereas A's Poipu base forces a ~2 hr round trip to Ke'e on arrival day 1 and a 3 hr 25 min drive day 7 for one garden. B mislabels Hanalei Pier 'at sunset' at 16:30 (sunset ~18:43) and neither plan mentions the Haena reservation, a Na Pali boat tour or hurricane season.

Both keep one Baixa/Chiado base and walkable days, and both omit Belem/Jeronimos entirely. A labels Sao Jorge 'at sunset' at 16:30 (sunset 20:40) and stacks lunch before the Time Out Market; B adds tram 28, Principe Real, a miradouro and Cervejaria Ramiro but double-books dinner on day 1 and schedules a 05:30 breakfast on departure day. Neither is meaningfully better.

A's Tenerife pick fits the request, but its plan is towns, churches and museums, with Teide left out by the plan's own admission, a 20:00 drive to Benijo beach after dark on arrival and a 2.5 hr round trip for one hour in Adeje. B's Turangi plan delivers restorative outdoor time (lake walks, waterfalls, Tokaanu and AC Baths hot pools, a boat trip). Its day-6 Red Crater/Emerald Lakes 'short drive' is impossible and too strenuous for children, and Bali in March (rainy season) weakens B's shortlist.

A drives Vik to Hofn on day 3 without stopping at Jokulsarlon (a hard requirement), puts Dyrholaey at 22:40 on 14 June while it is under nesting closure until about 23 June, and its day 4 has an incoherent ~10 hr Hofn-Akureyri leg; it does use the midnight sun well (Godafoss 23:10) and covers Myvatn and Husavik. B includes Jokulsarlon, Diamond Beach, Fjallsarlon, Vestrahorn and Hoffell but skips Myvatn and the south-coast waterfalls, has a 6 hr 10 min drive on day 5 and a pointless 05:30 'sunrise' start (sunrise ~02:26).

Both are single-base, rental-car plans, so neither offers multi-day inn-to-inn walking with luggage shuttles. A at least walks the family-friendly Hosshinmon-oji to Hongu Taisha section on day 3 (with a return-transport note) and covers all three Grand Shrines, Oyunohara and Yunomine. B has no Nakahechi walk beyond Daimon-zaka, fills days with scenic drives, mis-times 'sunset' stops at 16:30 and underestimates a Koyasan day trip as 70 min each way.

A's 'Song-Kol yurt camp' base is in Bishkek for all 10 nights: bazaars, museums, a nightclub, and Issyk-Kul stargazing scheduled at 18:00 before sunset. It has no trek, no yurt night and no Karakol. B at least spends four nights in Karakol (Jeti-Oguz, Altyn Arashan, Jyrgalan) and visits Kochkor's canyons. It still invents trains, has a broken 14-hour day-5 transfer, never actually sleeps at Song-Kol and has no multi-day trek.

Both use one Alta Badia/Corvara base and miss the Tre Cime circuit, Alpe di Siusi and the Braies/Auronzo reservations. A has stronger hikes (Nuvolau, Puez, Santa Croce), but its day 5 puts Seceda 'at sunrise' via a 35 min drive (the lifts open about 08:30), and day 4 has 3 hr+ of driving for Prato Piazza. B's Sassolungo circuit, Lago di Sorapis, Cinque Torri and Lagazuoi are top-tier and timed realistically, though it leans on scenic-drive filler.

A keeps one Tavira base but spends ~3 hr a day on trains and buses for thin content (Zoomarine and Albufeira at ~2 hr each way). It has only one beach day and no cave boat or clifftop viewpoints. B breaks the one-base rule (Lagos then Tavira) and adds a late 20:15 Cabo Sao Vicente run on arrival. It does deliver the defining Algarve: a Benagil boat trip, a three-beach Lagos day, Praia da Marinha and Algar Seco, Ilha de Tavira and Ilha Deserta. Both plans drop the grandparents from the party.

A is weak: it has no Serengeti and no Tarangire, Ngorongoro appears only as a 30-min flamingo stop and a truncated 05:30 departure-day drive, and it spends eight nights in Karatu. It does stay in the right region with an operator driver-guide. B is not a safari at all: from a 'Tarangire' base it sends the couple by bus to Dar es Salaam, Zanzibar Stone Town, Bagamoyo and Kizimkazi, which is geographically impossible.

A splits Shinjuku (4 nights) and Higashiyama (5) with the Shinkansen between. Tokyo gets Meiji Jingu, Shibuya, Shinjuku Gyoen blossom and teamLab; Kyoto gets dawn Fushimi Inari, Kiyomizu, Ginkaku-ji, Arashiyama, Kinkaku-ji and Nijo, all on transit (though Asakusa is missing). B never visits Tokyo, books a rental car for a train trip and drives everywhere in Kyoto, with several 05:30 starts.
